provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: In the native task, each seed cell of colour 3 gets a fixed gate motif. The motif has a 5-bar two cells before the seed, a 5-stub one cell before it, 2-walls at lateral offsets ±2, and an 8-floor two cells after it. A full-span line of colour 2 also passes through the floor offset. The factory turns each native offset vector into a visible offset vector. For d4 >= 4 it first negates dx (row reversal). It then applies (dy, dx) -> (dx, -dy) once for each clockwise rotation. Every motif colour is replaced by its palette constant. The floor offset (2, 0) is transformed too. If it points vertically, the emitted program draws a full visible row of palette[2]. Otherwise it draws a full visible column. The order matches the native solver: all lines are drawn first, then all motifs are stamped on top. Every write is bounds-checked. The emitted program works only in visible coordinates and does not rotate grids or remap colours.
draft_notes.limitations: This has not been tested; the host's verification is still to come. Seeds are found by exact match with palette[3], and every other cell is copied unchanged. The generator's domain guarantees that motifs and lines never collide with another seed's motif. If out-of-domain inputs did overlap, the precedence would follow the native order: lines first, then stamps in visible row-major seed order. That stamp order may differ from native row-major order under rotation, but only overlapping cases would be affected. Nothing in the fixtures contradicts the uniform rule.
